items.topic: Approving LAN pairing requests in pi-dashboard
items.fact: List pending: `GET /api/pair/pending` (fields pendingId, attemptsLeft, expiresAt ~5min, remoteAddress, userAgent). Approve: `POST /api/pair/approve-pending --data {pendingId, confirmCode (8 digits, no space), label, tier}`. Paired devices: `GET /api/paired-devices`. The code is shown only on the requester's screen. A wrong code consumes attempts (starts at 5). Tiers: control (chat only) vs operate (default; also spawn sessions, terminals, settings). Config `pairing.acceptLanRequests: true` enables Request access; no network trusted automatically. Approval covers whole dashboard, not just a session. Requester must keep the code page open until confirmed, else must re-request.

items.topic: Review-site chat uses dashboard embed view
items.fact: Review app chat panel default is 'Dashboard chat' loading `http://<host>:8000/session/<id>?embed=1` (host from page address); 'Simple chat' is the fallback tab. LAN colleagues request access and operator approves each; whether `observe` tier can send messages is unconfirmed.

Masks documented in data-access-guide.md 'Using Masks (Projections)' (line ~361-480): [Entity]Mask.entityMask().withX(); empty mask = existence check; nested masks for relationships; masks in dao.update for partial update; unmasked field access returns null with no error (most common bug; also Anti-Pattern 9 in integration-testing/best-practices.md). Operator asked for this, suggesting a discoverable mask how-to/best-practice entry in catalog/best-practices is missing (only agent-docs).

items.topic: Keep custom operation logic out of app module: osgi-service-layer-delegation
items.claim: Operator asked: 'Are there any practice for not write the custom operations java code on the app module use the dedicated common module for the services?'
items.fact: Blueprint osgi-service-layer-delegation covers it (BLUEPRINT.md + backend.md, 61 lines): interfaces as plain Java in common (no OSGi annotations), business-operation methods not CRUD, impl `@Component(immediate = true, service = X.class)` in module nearest concern (common, keycloak-client, firebase), custom operations in app/custom are thin delegators using `@Reference` on interfaces only; scheduler and interceptors reuse same services; plus I18n interface (AdTrackI18n with @MessageByKey, ThreadLocalLocaleSupplier, I18nService). Examples: indamedia-adtrack, mlszksz-platform, rackinspect. Note BLUEPRINT.md is thin and its listing points to backend.md; a best-practice entry likely missing.

items.topic: Per-reviewer isolated sessions via Keycloak, isolated Docker dashboard
items.fact: Operator chose Path A: Keycloak login + per-user isolation (users gabor/gabor-pw, mate/mate-pw), full green light for a FRESH dockerized Keycloak 26 plus Tailscale HTTPS; then proposed running a separate dashboard in isolated Docker. Operator: each reviewer copies (not mounts) review content into docker and sessions start from an initial prompt plus a skill, not a transcript. Each reviewer spawned via POST /api/session/spawn with cwd, model (@role), initialPrompt.

Dashboard identity plane (docs/identity-plane.md, identity-auth-plugin-guide.md): bundled keycloak-resolver validates tokens only; login UI needs a login descriptor from a trusted plugin (identity.trustedResolverPlugins). Config in ~/.pi/dashboard/config.json: identity.trustedResolverPlugins, trustedPolicyPlugin, resolverTimeoutMs, policyTimeoutMs. Enforced: session owner must equal requester principal, non-owner sessions invisible. Keycloak public PKCE client needs redirectUris `<origin>/callback` and `/*`, webOrigins = dashboard origin; http issuer needs allowInsecureHttp:true; tailscale serve HTTPS recommended and Keycloak should be HTTPS too. Break-glass: `pi-dashboard login --local`. Loopback operator always admitted. Bearer held in memory only, no refresh token.

pi-agent-dashboard/docker/ has Dockerfile and compose*.yml. A containerized dashboard is a separate instance with no host sessions. Mounting ~/.pi/agent exposes credentials/settings/extensions/sessions; alternatives: host credential proxy or dedicated auth.json. Dashboard gateway socket not reachable from container; pi needs write on agent dir, ~/.pi/context-mode/sessions.
